_comment: Detector parameter presets for the Kalibr AprilGrid (36h11). Edit this file to add or tune a
preset; no Python changes needed. Any name here is valid for Calibration.py --preset.
Keys are cv2.aruco.DetectorParameters attribute names and are validated on load, so a typo
fails immediately instead of being silently ignored.
board_params describe the TARGET, not the tuning, so they are merged into every preset.
Measured on 12 left frames of the 18 Sep set, omitting them is silent and severe:
markerBorderBits at its default of 1 drops tags found from 403 to 201, and errorCorrectionRate
at its default of 0.6 drops it to 350. A preset that redefined them from scratch once found zero.
A preset may still override one, but make_detector() warns when it does.
Do not set adaptiveThreshConstant to 0 (as the UWAruco paper does) on this footage: it collapses
detection, 403 -> 43 tags on the same sample, because these tags are low-contrast rather than
dark, so subtracting nothing from the local mean thresholds most of the tag to white.

wide._why: 3..53 sweep for tags that range from tiny and far to filling the frame, plus a lowered Otsu floor for low-contrast underwater tags.

uwaruco._why: Window sizes from the UWAruco paper (10/20/40), without its adaptiveThreshConstant=0.

opencv_default._why: No thresholding tuning at all. A reference point the others have to beat.

water_sweep_from_wide._why: Coordinate-descent sweep from 'wide' by sweep_detector.py: 10424 distinct board tags over 187 usable images, 0.21% wrong detections.

water_sweep_from_default._why: Coordinate-descent sweep from 'opencv_default' by sweep_detector.py: 10424 distinct board tags over 187 usable images, 0.21% wrong detections.

water_final._why: Underwater sweep result (water_sweep_from_default, identical from wide) with polygonalApproxAccuracyRate put back to 0.03. The sweep picked 0.08 for +42 tags, but on 8 Oct that loose outline fit moved 39% of corners >2 px from where wide put them and raised calibration RMS to 5-8 px; at 0.03 it is 0.7% for 1.3% fewer tags.
